blocks.x: In Indian culture the beginning of every auspicious ceremony is done with the blowing of conch as the sound of it purifies the environment. The meaning of Shankh (conch) is expression of determination. In mythology it is symbol of energy so it is very significant to blow conch during worshipping ceremony. Churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) is one of the best known episodes in Hindu mythology. All kinds of herbs were cast into the ocean and fourteen Ratnas (gems or treasures) were produced from the ocean and Shankh is one of these Ratnas. Lord Krishna reverberated the whole world by blowing a conch (shankh) during Mahabharata.
Conch - An Introduction

Conch is symbol of wealth. By placing it at place of worship at home it eradicates misfortunes and enhances destiny. Conch is beneficial for the fulfilment of desires and it is considered as sibling of Goddess Laxmi. The conch which is held in right hand is termed as Dakshinavarti and the one to which we hold in left hand is Vamavarti. Both these are comparatively more precious as they are miraculous and rare.

Conch serves its worshipper for rising financially. It is a symbol of glory, reputation, victory & Laxmi therefore; it is used extensively during all religious ceremonies including establishing Shivling, construction of temple, Rudrabhishek, Arti, Hawan, religious function, house warming ceremony, vastudosh rectification and Pitra Tarpan etc.

Apart from above mentioned Anushthaanas it is also used for getting other benefits. By establishing it in shop, office, house and factory etc it heals Vastu related faults and brings the blessings of Goddess Laxmi for the progress of business. Conch is generally placed near the feet of Gods. By establishing Dakshinavarti conch at place of worship one attains stable wealth.

For the fulfilment of desires a pair of male and female conch should be kept at place of worship. Offer water to a pregnant woman from Ganesh Conch daily she would give birth to healthy child. Establishing Turtle Conch blesses with food, grains and wealth. Similarly if you have ‘Moti Conch’ at home the Goddess Saubhagya Laxmi shall ever bless you with fortune.

It is considered highly auspicious to do Rudrabhishekam of lord Shiva with conch. All types of conches can be used to offer Arghya to Sun. As per astrological and Tantrik references the conches of various names and shapes are used for the accomplishment of all sorts of objectives. Influence of conch never lessens. It makes no difference if a man blows either a big or small conch.
All religious ceremonies are started with the blowing of conch. In Hindu religion it is considered as the primary object of making prayer.
Significance of Conch

The sound of the shankha symbolises the sacred Om sound. Vishnu holding the conch represents him as the god of sound. Brahma Vaivarta Purana declares that shankha is the residence of both Lakshmi and Vishnu, bathing by the waters led through a shankha is considered as like bathing with all holy waters at once. Sankha Sadma Purana declares that bathing an image of Vishnu with cow milk is as virtuous as performing a million yajnas (fire sacrifices), and bathing Vishnu with Ganges river water frees one from the cycle of births.

It further says "while the mere sight of the conch (shankha) dispels all sins as the Sun dispels the fog, why talk of its worship?" Padma Purana asserts the same effect of bathing Vishnu by Ganges water and milk and further adds doing so avoids evil, pouring water from a shankha on one's own head before a Vishnu image is equivalent to bathing in the pious Ganges river.

In Buddhism, the conch shell has been incorporated as one of the eight auspicious symbols, also called Ashtamangala. The right-turning white conch shell, Wylie- dung gyas 'khyil), represents the elegant, deep, melodious, interpenetrating and pervasive sound of Buddhism, which awakens disciples from the deep slumber of ignorance and urges them to accomplish their own welfare and the welfare of others.
Shankha was the Royal State Emblem of Travancore and also figured on the Royal Flag of the Jaffna kingdom. It is also the election symbol of the Indian political party Biju Janata Dal.
Conch - A Dwelling Place of Deities
Conch shell is said to be the abode of many deities i. e.

Moon dwells at the base of conch shell, Varuna in the Kukshi, Prajapati on the back of the conch and Ganga-Saraswati at the mouth. O Panchjanya, you arose from the ocean and Lord Vishnu has held you in his hand. You are ahead among the gods, hence I salute you.
So mere Darshana of conch liberates from sins, eradicates poverty, enhances longevity and brings prosperity.
Significance of Conch in Fengshui

From Fengshui view point the conch, (shell) attracts business and benefits from overseas connections. The conch is one of the eight auspicious symbols found on the foot of Lord Buddha. Conch is considered very auspicious for export business. For getting name and fame it should be kept in Southern direction of living room.
In North-East direction it is auspicious for good results in education and in South West direction it energies your good luck for relationship.
Conch as Symbol of Power
In ancient India every man used to keep a conch with him, which he used during different times to declare his presence and power.
In Mahabharata there is a detailed description of all the conches that the different warriors blew before the starting of the great war.

Every conch has its specific name. The conch of Vishnu is Panchjanya and the names of conches of Arjuma, Bheema, Yudhishthara, Nakula and Sahdev are Devdatt, Pondra, Anantvijaya, Sughosha and Manipushpaka respectively.
In Hindu legend

A Hindu legend in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana recalls the creation of conchs- Shiva flung a trident towards the asuras, burning them instantaneously. Their ashes flew in the sea creating conchs. Shankha is believed to be a brother of Lakshmi as both of them were born from the sea. A legend describes an asura named Shankhasura, who was killed by Vishnu's fish avatar, Matsya.

In the Hindu epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata, the symbol of Shankha is widely adopted. In the Ramayana epic, Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna are considered as part-incarnations of Sheshanaga, Sudarshana Chakra and Shankha, respectively, while Rama, their eldest brother, is considered as one of the ten Avatars of shri Vishnu.

During the great Mahabharata war, Krishna, as the charioteer of the Pandava prince and a protagonist of the epic - Arjuna - resounds the Panchajanya to declare war. Panchajanya in Sanskrit means 'having control over the five classes of beings'. All five Pandava brothers are described having their own shankhas. Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva are described to possess shankhas named Ananta-Vijaya, Poundra-Khadga, Devadatta, Sughosha and Mani-pushpaka, respectively.

The ancient text Brahmavaivart Purana contains deep knowledge related to the different forms of Goddess Laxmi. In this Purana it is described that Saubhagya Laxmi who brings good luck is present in Moti Shankh. In other words if you have ‘Moti Conch’ at home the Goddess Saubhagya Laxmi shall ever bless you with fortune.

It is believed that 'Moti Shankh’ is more important and miraculous than 'Dakshinavarti Shank' because it is rare and difficult to find. With the worship of Moti Shankh success comes rapidly. It is stated everywhere in Hindu mythology that conch brings money and fame.

Early Hinduism classified the conch into male and female varieties with the thicker shelled bulbous conch occurring as the male or purusha and the thin shelled slender conch as the female or Shankhini. The fourfold caste division was also applied, with the smooth white conch representing the Brahmin caste, the red conch the Kshatriya of warrior caste, the yellow conch the Vaishya or merchant caste, and the dull grey conch the Shudra or labourer caste.
Association with Nagas (Snakes)

Because of the association of the shankha with water, nāgas are often named after the shankha. The list of Nāgas in the Mahabharata, the Harivamsha and the Bhagavat Purana includes names like Shankha, Mahashankha, Shankhapala and Shankachuda. The last two are also mentioned in the Buddhist Jataka Tales and the Jimutavahana. A legend states that while using Shankha as part of meditative ritual, a sadhu blew his shankha in the forest of village Keoli and a snake crept out of it. The snake directed the

sadhu that he should be worshipped as Nāga Devata (Serpent god) and since then it has been known as Shanku Naga. Similar legends are narrated at many other places in Kullu district in Himachal Pradesh.
Ayurvedic and Scientific Significance of Conch

Blowing the conch is a part of daily rituals for performing the worshipping ceremonies in temples and in houses. The significance of conch is no less in Ayurveda of Dhanvantari. It is believed that blowing the conch daily saves a man from heart diseases. The process of blowing a conch gives one a better health and specially improves the respiratory system. Blowing of conch gives relief in throat related diseases. As per Ayurveda the Shankohdak ash cures stomach related diseases and purifies blood.

Shankha is used in Ayurveda medicinal formulations to treat many ailments. Conch is blown to purify the environment specially while performing worshipping ceremonies. Even the scientists have agreed the fact that the blowing of a conch increases the positive qualities in the atmosphere such as courage, hope, determination, will power, optimism etc.
Scientific Basis of Conch Sound

As per scientists the sound of conch creates an impact on the environment. The bacteria and diseases of the area reached by conch sound get killed completely. As per Brahmvaivarat Puraan water should be poured in a conch placed in a temple and sprinkled everywhere in the house to fill it with positive energy.

When water is kept in a pot of metal then it consumes the qualities of metal, similarly, when kept in conch it consumes the good qualities of conch and the sprinkling of same water on human body protects the person from infectious diseases and the bacteria get killed.
Scientific Significance
If conch is taken near the ears then very light sound that of sea waves can be heard. The vibrations created from the sound of conch block the negative and destructive powers on earth.

In addition to that it can also protect from pollution and global warming. It fills the holes in ozone layer. As per the revelation of a scientific study the blowing of a conch increases the positive qualities in the atmosphere such as courage, hope, determination, will power, optimism etc.
Folklore on Conch

The sound of conch frightens the animals and therefore the dangerous creatures like snakes etc do not create obstacles in the meditational practices of devotees. It is also believed that evil spirits run away from the sound of conch. Because of these qualities of conch there is a tradition of blowing conch in eastern India at the time of natural calamities and earthquakes. The main feeling behind this is to call the protector of the universe for getting protection.
Medicinal Significance of Conch

As per Ayurveda the conch has special medicinal significance. Carefully made medicines from the ash of conch protect from several diseases. Shankha is used in Ayurveda medicinal formulations to treat many ailments. It is prepared as conch shell ash, known in Sanskrit as shankha bhasma, which is prepared by soaking the shell in lime juice and calcinating in covered crucibles, 10 to 12 times, and finally reducing it to powder ash. Shankha bhasma contains calcium, iron and magnesium and is considered to possess antacid and digestive properties.

A compound pill called shankavati is also prepared for use in dyspepsia. In this case, the procedure followed is to mix shankha bhasma with tamarind seed ash, five salts (panchlavana), asafoetida, ammonium chloride, pepper, carui, caraway, ginger, long pepper, purified mercury and aconite in specified proportions. It is then triturated in juices of lemon and made into a pill-mass. It is prescribed for vata (wind/air) and pitta (bile) ailments, as well as for beauty and strength.
The regular practice of blowing of conch during Yoga sadhana strengthens the trachea. It cures heart diseases and enhances immunity.

The all religious beliefs associated with conch have scientific basis. Scientists believe that the radiation of Sun creates obstacles in the broadcasting of sound. Therefore the suitable time for blowing conch is considered early morning and evening when the density of the radiations of Sun is not much. The sound of conch can kill the bacteria of all infectious diseases.

The Indian scientist Jagdish Chander Bose has proved this fact with the help of experiments. The sound of conch also heals the problem of stammering and deafness. One who blows conch regularly gets relief from problems like breathlessnesss, asthma and diseases of lungs.
In nutshell the sound of conch can heal several diseases. The regular practice of blowing of conch purifies the environment. It is believed that the blowing
of conch is a declaration of victory of Punya (good, auspicious, morality) over Paap (bad, inauspicious, sin).
Worshipping Conch

Conch is the symbol of God. Its Abhishekam (sprinkling ceremony) is done with milk, Ghee, honey, jaggery, etc. It should be wrapped in red cloth and worshipped with Dhoop, Deep & Naivedya in an auspicious Muhurat on the day of Dipawali, Holi, Navratri, Ramnavami, Gurupushya Yoga or Friday. By doing this one gets rid off chronic diseases, poverty and sorrow.
Conch for Favourable Vastu

The conch should be placed in the north east corner of the house in such a way so that the face of the conch remains towards north. It enhances happiness, wealth and love among family members and their health remains good. In addition to that it proves highly auspicious for the continuous upgradation of education along with the mental balance of all family members. By offering Tulsi leaves to conch all types of Siddhis can be attained but remember it should not be done on Sunday.

The north east corner is most important direction in the house therefore by placing a Dakshinavarti conch containing Gangajal in this direction one can attain the permanent blessings of goddess of wealth.

In this way the systematic establishment and regular worship of conch results in the attainment of happiness, prosperity, longevity and wealth alongwith capable sons. Probably that is why only it has been affirmed that-
Goddess Laxmi never leaves the place where conch is blown."
The best quality conches are found in Maldweep, Kailash Mansarovar, Andeman and Nikobar Islands, Srilanka, Arabian sea, Pacific ocean and Indian ocean.
Types of Conch
Conches are of several types out of which the main two are as follows-
Dakshinavarti Conch 1.
Vamavarti Conch 2.
Dakshinavarti Conch

That conch which opens towards right side is known as Dakshinavarti conch. It is a very rare conch of white colour with brown lines on it. The direction of god of wealth Kuber is south therefore, it is termed as a symbol of money,
wealth and prosperity. Its shape is that of a grain of wheat and size can be as big as coconut.
Vamavarti Conch

that conch which opens towards left side is termed as vamavarti conch. It is easily available conch and can be used in all religious activities. Most of the conches are Vamavarti. The astrologers recommend the use of these conches for the elimination of all negative energies. By blowing this conch all negative energies get eradicated and the soul and the atmosphere around becomes purified.

blocks.x: Dakshinavarti Conch

This conch comes from deep seas. It is indeed a form of Narayana because Laxmi and Vishnu both love it. Both of them keep this in their hands. Goddess Durga too holds it in her hand. Wherever there is a Dakshinavarti Conch Goddess Durga, Laxmi and Vishnu dwell at that place. Water and leaves of Basil kept for 24 hrs in this conch turn the water as holy as Ganga Jal.
Dakshinavarti

A man may have blessings of Lord Vishnu if he takes daily the water kept in it. The conch showers its auspicious effect on a business person if he keeps and worships it at place of worship, shop, godown etc.

Dakshinavarti conch is the symbol of Goddess Laxmi. This conch is used to bring good luck and prosperity to the family. This is a sea shell which opens towards right hand and is very rare with lot of spiritual significance; it is used to purify the environment from evil effects. Dakshinavarti conch is used to get luck, windfall gains, acquisition of wealth and unforeseen gains. Generally conches are easily available but Dakshinavarti conch is different and rare.
Ganesha Conch

This conch is obtained from the sea. The figure of Ganesha remains embossed on it naturally. Establishment of this shell at place of worship brings the blessings of Lord Ganesha. Peace and prosperity prevails at home. The hurdles in achieving endeavours are removed. By worshipping it one gets wealth, success, intelligence and the malefic effects of Rahu get sublimated. This conch increases the strength of character and Ganesh Conch mind and help achieve happiness, fame, good health and increases confidence. This conch is said to represent Lord Ganesha. This is especially used in worship. Worshippers of this gets long life and they become truthful. It also gives better ability and talent for studies.

By worshipping it one remains free from diseases, becomes intelligent and does not experience hurdles in tasks. It is beneficial and helpful in betting, house racing and lotteries etc. Worship of this conch is beneficial for getting the blessings of Ganesha.

Ganesha Conch is a very effective item for getting protection from evil effects. So, every house should have this conch for the protection of it from evil effects and to get wealth, prosperity and good luck.

By worshipping it there won’t be any shortage of food, money or clothes. It brings peace to the premises. If kept in the bedroom, it brings harmony among the couple. If kept during a religious gathering, it brings knowledge by evoking lord Ganesha. It enlightens the students with knowledge and sharpens their memory. Fill it with the holy water of Ganges and sprinkle it on a person or in a premises to get protection from malefic planetary effects and black magic. Removes sins accrued by killing of a priest, cow or a child in the previous births.
Ganesha conch should be established on Monday in Morning after washing it with raw milk and clean water and by worshiping it with Dhoop-Deep (incense and lamp)
Turtle Conch
This conch is naturally shaped like a tortoise. Keeping this conch at place

of worship and paying respect to it removes hurdles coming in the path of family progress. Wealth and prestige are obtained. Conch symbolizes money, fame and benefits from overseas connections and turtle symbolises long life. Therefore turtle conch attracts wealth, glory and gains from foreign land. It is also believed that tortoise lifted the weight of the earth over its back. In relation to lord Kachhap avtar (incarnation of Lord Vishnu) it is also believed that the whole energy and substance of this living world or earth is created around Meru Prishth (back of tortoise) Turtle Conch which has the elements like water, earth along with mountains.

So from this we come to know that what is the importance, significance and the reason of miraculous impact of symbol of tortoise. Tortoise alone in itself is considered to be an auspicious symbol of good luck in Hindu mythology.

Vastushastra, Chinese Astrology & Fengshui has also accepted its importance. This turtle conch shall also work as a Vastu correction tool also. This should be established on Monday or Friday in the morning after clearing it with the holy water of Gangajal and raw milk.
Pearl Conch
Pearl conch known as Moti Shankh is very rare spiritual item. Conch serves
its worshipper for progressing financially. This conch enhances destiny and helps to attract business and benefits from overseas connections. This also brings name and fame to you.

The ancient text Brahmavevart Puran contains deep knowledge related to the different forms of Goddess Laxmi. It is described that Saubhagya Laxmi who brings good luck is present in Moti Shankh. In other words if Pearl Conch have 'Pearl Conch' at home the Goddess Saubhagya Laxmi shall ever bless you with fortune.

It is believed that 'Pearl conch' is more important and miraculous than 'Dakshinavarti Shankh' because it is rare and difficult to find. With the worship of this conch success comes faster. It shall also give mental peace, power of intuition and blessings of Goddess to its worshipper.
Conch for Blowing
Lord Krishna reverberated the whole world by blowing a conch during

Mahabharata. It is believed that blowing a conch daily saves a man from heart diseases. In ancient India every man used to keep a conch with him whom he used during different times to declare his presence and power.

In Mahabharata there is a detailed description of all the conch that the Blowing Conch different warriors blew before the starting of the Great war. Blowing the conch while performing the worshipping ceremonies in temples and houses is a part of daily rituals.
The process of blowing of a conch gives one a better health and specially improves the respiratory system. Conch is blown to purify the environment specially while performing worshipping ceremonies.
Even the scientists have agreed the fact that the blowing of a conch increases the positive qualities in the atmosphere such as courage, hope, determination, will-power, optimism etc.
Gomukhi Conch
This conch resembles the face of a cow that is why it is named as Go - Cow,

Mukhi - Face. Cow is the sacred animal of Hindus. Worshipping Gomukhi conch is equal to worshipping a cow. This is also known as Kamdhenu Shankh. The best quality spotless, neat and clean glittering conches are found in Mansarovar, bay of Bengal, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nikobar Islands, Srilanka, Arabian sea, and Indian ocean.
Gomukhi Conch The weight of natural Gomukhi conch of Mansarovar generally ranges from 500 gms to 3 Kg. It is used in the treatment of incurable diseases.
Vishnu Conch
Laxmi stays in that house where Shri Hari Vishnu stays. Therefore, Goddess

Lakshmi and Narayan stay in that house where Vishnu Shankh (symbol of Vishnu) is established. It is believed that by pouring Gangajal in this conch in Rohini, Chitra & Swati Nakshatra and then offering that water to a pregnant woman she gives birth to an attractive, intelligent and healthy child.

It looks like Garuda (vehicle of Lord Vishnu). In Shastras it has been given Vishnu Conch the name of Chandra Shankh. If a pregnant woman drinks water kept in conch then her children do not suffer from diseases of lungs. This conch is used to gain progress in business and to overcome poverty.

Chant the Mantra of this conch on a rosary of conch 108 times and establish it in a business unit or in a building in north east corner and chant the Mantra 5 times again. Do the 3 Achmani (sip 3 times) and then sprinkle at business house. Worshipping this conch overcomes any type of troubles related to house, health, family and business etc. Issues like obstacles in begetting children, incurable diseases or slow progress in business get rectified by worshipping it daily. The house having Vishnu conch blesses the resident with all material comforts and finally salvation. This is a panacea for those suffering from heart related troubles. Fill conch with water in moon light at night and drink next morning and do it daily the problems like heart attack etc shall get cured.
Annapurna Conch

Annapurna conch is used for the development of destiny and attainment of prosperity. Fill it with Gangajal and drink that water in the morning to fill mentally satisfy and fit. It overcomes problems like impatience and restlessness. Among all conches the Annapurna Conch is heaviest. The average weight of this conch ranges from 3kg to 9kg. This conch looks very beautiful. Write your name on the leaf of Aak and place Annapurna Annapurna conch on it and chant following Mantra 108 times daily and do it Conch continuously for 21 days. This is best Anushthan for Annapurna Siddhi. The house having Annapurna Conch is considered full of Annam (grains), Dhanam (money), Saubhagyam (good luck) and all round development. The devotee of Annapunra Conch should use it all auspicious, religious ceremonies like marriage, religious Anushthan, Yagya and charity etc.
Panchjanya Conch
Panchajanya is the conch of the Hindu god Vishnu. As per Valmiki
Ramyana, Purushottama (Vishnu) killed a Danava named Panchajana on a mountain named Chakravan constructed by Vishwakarma and took away conch shell known as Panchajanya from him.

As per Harivamsa, Krishna, the avatar of Vishnu, is described possessing a shankha called Panchajanya, one of his four attributes together with the Panchjanya mace Kaumodaki, the disc-like weapon Sudarshana Chakra and a lotus Conch flower. The conch was used during the Kurukshetra War. Panchajanya or Shankhasur was an evil sea demon who lived in a colossal conch shell in the deepest depths of the Prabhasa Ocean or was a demon in the form of a conch shell.

He kidnapped the son of Sandipani, the Guru of Shri Krishna, Balarama and Sudama and imprisoned him in the conch shell. Upon completion of their studies, Krishna, Balarama, and Sudama persuaded the teacher to ask for the preceptor’s Dakshina of his liking. Sandipani asked for, as his dakshina, the restoration of his child. Krishna became enraged when he heard about the kidnap and plunged into the sea to rescue the son of Sandipani. Krishna successfully slew Shankhasur and took the conch shell for himself. He then named the conch shell after the Demon. Whenever Krishna blows from the shell it foreshadows the death of his next opponent.

It looks like Vamavarti Shankh and has the image of five fingers on it and that is why at times it is also termed as Panchanguli Shankh. It is very effective in the rectification of Vastu faults. In addition to that it should be used by politicians as it brings success in winning elections and legal cases.

It overcomes obstacles, enemies, Shani Conch accidents and poverty etc and life becomes easier.
